名.meaning: In the <part>evening</part> dark you can't see who's coming up the path. So a <part>mouth</part> calls out into the night, and a voice answers with one word: who they are. In the dark you only know them by their <kanji>name</kanji>.
名.on: Lost in a hedge <sound>ma</sound>ze at night, you shout your name until a friend finds you.
名.kun: Your friend holds up a warm <sound>na</sound>an with your name written on it.

二.meaning: Two planks stacked, the top one short and the bottom one long, like a bunk bed for sticks. The short stick sleeps on top, the long one underneath. Count the sleepers: <kanji>two</kanji>.
二.on: Both sticks are sewn to their bunks with a single sewing <sound>nee</sound>dle so they can't roll out.
二.kun: The two sticks share one <sound>fu</sound>ton and one <sound>ta</sound>co for breakfast.

発.meaning: A <part>tent</part> folds up its flaps, and under it <part>two</part> planks on a pair of <part>legs</part> start running. The whole campsite packs up and sprints for the bus. Time for <kanji>departure</kanji>!
発.on: The campers burst out of their <sound>huts</sound> before sunrise.
発.kun: Each camper grabs one <sound>ta</sound>co for the road, and the bus pulls out.

水.meaning: Drop a stone into a pond and this is the splash: a tall spout shooting up the middle, drops flying out to the left and right. Your shoes are soaked. It's <kanji>water</kanji>.
水.on: A wrapped <sound>swee</sound>t falls into the pond and fizzes in the water.
水.kun: A <sound>mee</sound>rkat squirts water at a bee, which buzzes off with a short, cross '<sound>Zu</sound>!'

土.meaning: A post sticks up out of a long, flat field, a short crossbar nailed near its top. Pull it up and clumps of brown dirt cling to its bottom. Plant your seeds around it in the <kanji>soil</kanji>.
土.on: A <sound>do</sound>lphin flops onto the field and digs in the soil, very confused.
土.kun: The dust makes you sneeze, '<sound>Tsu</sound>!', right in a sleeping <sound>chee</sound>tah's face.

場.meaning: On a patch of bare <part>soil</part>, <part>sunbeams</part> pour down through the clouds onto one bright spot. Here's where the picnic goes. Spread the blanket in the light and mark it: the perfect <kanji>location</kanji>.
場.on: A <sound>jo</sound>ey hops in and claims the spot before anyone else.
場.kun: '<sound>Bah</sound>!' grumbles a man who wanted that very spot.

寸.meaning: A <part>golf club</part> swings down past a tiny ball. Missed by a hair! The golfer crouches and checks the gap with a ruler: exactly one thumb's width. He writes down the <kanji>measurement</kanji>.
寸.on: His caddie offers him a roll of <sound>su</sound>shi, but he's too busy measuring and only mutters '<sound>Nn</sound>.'

時.meaning: Every morning the <part>sun</part> clocks in at the <part>temple</part>, punching its card in the machine by the door. One day it oversleeps and rolls in at noon, still yawning. The head monk taps his watch: 'And what <kanji>time</kanji> do you call this?'
時.on: A <sound>jee</sound>p honks at the monk: 'Hurry up, your time is up!'
時.kun: On a <sound>to</sound>tem pole by the gate hangs a big brass <sound>key</sound> to wind the clock.
